chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Does the menstruating woman make up the fast?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'Does she make up the prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said, 'From where does this come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The first one to analogise was Iblees.'
ai.seo_question: Why do menstruating women make up their missed fasts but not their missed prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction where menstruating women are exempt from making up missed prayers but must compensate for missed fasting. The Imam attributes this ruling to the principle of qiyas (analogy), identifying Iblees as the first to employ it, thereby linking the legal exception to a theological origin story found in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The menstruating woman would make up for the (missed) Fast?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘She would make up for the (missed) Prayer?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: No. ‘I said, ‘Where does this come from?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The first one to analogise was Iblees<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Rashid who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if a woman experiencing Hayd (menses) is required to complete Qada’ (compensatory fast) of the fast. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, she is required to complete its Qada’ (compensatory fast).’ I then asked if she is required to perform Qada’ (compensatory salat) of Salat (prayer)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, she is not required to perform Qada’ (compensatory salat) for Salat (prayer).’ I then asked, ‘On what basis is it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The first one who analogized was Iblis (Satan).”’
